s: A company is developing a solution to analyze images. The solution uses a 50 TB reference dataset and analyzes images up to 1 TB in size. The solution spreads requests across an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 Linux instances in a VPC. The EC2 instances are attached to shared Amazon EBS io2 volumes in each Availability Zone. The EBS volumes store the reference dataset. During testing, multiple parallel analyses led to numerous disk errors, which caused job failures. The company wants the solution to provide seamless data reading for all instances. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
o: Create a new EBS volume for each EC2 instance. Copy the data from the shared volume to the new EBS volume regularly. Update the application to reference the new EBS volume.

Move all the reference data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Install Mountpoint for Amazon S3 on the EC2 instances. Create gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 in the VPC. Replace the EBS mount point with the S3 mount point.

Move all the reference data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an Amazon S3 backed Multi-AZ Amazon EFS volume. Mount the EFS volume on the EC2 instances. Replace the EBS mount point with the EFS mount point.
Upgrade the instances to local storage. Copy the data from the shared EBS volume to the local storage regularly. Update the application to reference the local storage.
x: The reference data is only read, so S3 plus Mountpoint for Amazon S3 (with a gateway endpoint) gives every instance parallel read access at S3 prices. EFS doesn't come in an 'S3-backed' form (C), and a 50 TB EFS file system costs far more than S3.

w.y: The 50 TB reference data is only read, and the disk errors come from sharing io2 Multi-Attach volumes without a cluster-aware file system. Storing the data in Amazon S3 and mounting it with Mountpoint for Amazon S3 gives every instance high-throughput parallel reads at S3 prices. A gateway endpoint keeps the traffic private at no extra cost.

o.A: Per-instance copies of 50 TB on EBS multiply storage cost and add copy and sync effort.
o.B: Correct: Mountpoint is built for large parallel read workloads on S3, the cheapest place for 50 TB of shared data.
o.C: EFS doesn't come in an 'S3-backed' form, and 50 TB on EFS costs far more than S3.
o.D: Instance store is ephemeral and would need regular 50 TB copies to each instance, which is costly and fragile.

s: Mount an Amazon S3 bucket as a local file system
Attach an EBS volume to multiple EC2 instances using Multi-Attach
